## Detailed Findings

#### 1. Kilocode JetBrains timeline navigation MEDIUM ~6-8h (TUI, navigation)

- **What**: Kilocode PR #14926 (merged 2026-10-09) adds JetBrains timeline navigation to transcript parts. Commit title: "fix(jetbrains): navigate to transcript parts from the session timeline". JetBrains IDE plugin shows a session timeline (sidebar list of tool calls + messages chronologically). User clicks timeline item, IDE scrolls transcript to that message/tool. Implementation: timeline stores message/tool IDs, click handler calls `scrollToTranscriptPart(id)`, transcript widget scrolls to element with matching `data-id` attribute. Alexi TUI has no timeline widget — transcript is single scrolling view with no index/sidebar.

- **Why**: Alexi TUI renders transcript in `MessageArea.tsx` or `MessageBubble.tsx` (marked + marked-terminal, full scrolling list). Long sessions (50+ messages, 20+ tool calls) are hard to navigate — user must scroll manually to find earlier tool/message. Kilocode pattern: (1) build timeline data structure (array of `{id, type, timestamp, label}` for each message/tool in session), (2) render timeline as sidebar list (Ink `<Box>` with vertical layout, each item clickable), (3) on click, emit scroll event with target message ID, (4) MessageArea listens for scroll event, finds matching message element, calls `scrollIntoView` or manual offset calculation. MEDIUM ~6-8h: (1) add timeline component (Ink sidebar with message/tool list, highlight current item), (2) extract message IDs from session state, (3) implement click handler emits scroll-to-message event, (4) wire MessageArea to receive event + scroll to target (may need ref-based scroll or manual offset calculation since Ink has no native `scrollIntoView`), (5) add keybind (e.g. Ctrl+T toggles timeline visibility), (6) test timeline click scrolls to correct message. Consider deferring if Ink scroll control is complex — Ink rendering is DOM-less, manual scroll offset calculation required.

- **Source**: https://github.com/Kilo-Org/kilocode/pull/14926 (JetBrains timeline navigation), /home/runner/work/alexi/alexi/src/cli/tui/components/MessageArea.tsx (transcript rendering), /home/runner/work/alexi/alexi/src/cli/tui/context/KeybindContext.tsx (keybind registry)

- **Category**: tool (TUI, navigation)

- **Size**: MEDIUM ~6-8h (add timeline component with message/tool list, extract IDs from session, implement click handler + scroll event, wire MessageArea scroll-to-message, add Ctrl+T keybind, test click scrolls correctly, manual scroll offset calculation for Ink)

#### 2. Kilocode transcript pruning cache SMALL ~3-4h (core, performance)

- **What**: Kilocode PR #14816 (merged 2026-10-09) reuses loaded transcript when pruning large payloads. Commit title: "fix(cli): reuse the loaded transcript when pruning large payloads". When context limit exceeded, pruning logic loaded transcript from disk, computed tokens, pruned, then saved. Orchestrator already loaded same transcript earlier in the turn. Double-read is slow for large sessions (50+ messages, 100+ KB JSON). Fix: pass loaded transcript to pruning function instead of file path, pruning operates on in-memory structure, saves result. Avoids second disk read.

- **Why**: Alexi orchestrator in `src/core/orchestrator.ts` or `streamingOrchestrator.ts` loads session transcript at start of turn, passes messages to provider. When context limit exceeded, check if pruning logic re-loads transcript from disk (grep for `readFile` or `loadSession` in pruning path). Kilocode pattern: (1) orchestrator loads transcript once, (2) passes in-memory transcript to pruning function instead of session ID, (3) pruning operates on passed structure, (4) orchestrator saves pruned result. Alexi equivalent: audit orchestrator context-limit handling (`src/core/orchestrator.ts` L200-400 likely), identify if transcript is re-loaded during pruning, refactor pruning to accept in-memory messages array instead of session path, save pruned result from orchestrator. SMALL ~3-4h: audit orchestrator pruning path, identify double-read (if exists), refactor pruning function signature (accept messages array instead of session ID), update call site to pass loaded messages, verify no disk re-read, test context limit triggers pruning without performance regression.

- **Source**: https://github.com/Kilo-Org/kilocode/pull/14816 (transcript pruning cache), /home/runner/work/alexi/alexi/src/core/orchestrator.ts (orchestrator, context limit handling), /home/runner/work/alexi/alexi/src/core/streamingOrchestrator.ts (streaming orchestrator)

- **Category**: core (performance, session management)

- **Size**: SMALL ~3-4h (audit orchestrator context-limit handling for double-read, refactor pruning to accept in-memory messages, update call site, test no performance regression)

#### 3. Kilocode Bedrock tool-result images MEDIUM ~4-6h (provider, Bedrock)

- **What**: Kilocode PR #14524 (merged 2026-10-09) sends tool-result images as user content for Bedrock GPT-6 models. Commit title: "fix(cli): send tool-result images as user content for Bedrock GPT-6 models". Bedrock GPT-6 (Amazon Nova) rejects tool-result messages containing images (HTTP 400 "tool results cannot contain images"). Kilocode detects Bedrock GPT-6 model ID prefix (`us.amazon.nova`, `eu.amazon.nova`, `ap.amazon.nova`), moves image content blocks from tool-result message to next user message. If no user message follows, appends synthetic user message with image + caption "Continuing the conversation". Other models (Claude, GPT-4, Gemini) accept tool-result images unchanged.

- **Why**: Alexi has Bedrock provider (`src/providers/` likely has `bedrock.ts` or references in `sapOrchestration.ts`). Audit if Bedrock Nova models are supported (check `modelCatalog.ts` or `model-match.ts` for `amazon.nova` prefix). Kilocode pattern: (1) detect model family (regex `us\.amazon\.nova|eu\.amazon\.nova|ap\.amazon\.nova`), (2) scan messages for tool-result with image content blocks, (3) move images to next user message or create synthetic user message, (4) preserve tool-result text, (5) send transformed messages to provider. Alexi equivalent: audit Bedrock provider message transform logic (`src/providers/transform.ts` L100-200 likely), add model-specific image placement (check if model is Bedrock Nova, apply image move transform), test with mock Bedrock Nova response (tool-result with image returns 400, transformed request succeeds). MEDIUM ~4-6h IF Alexi supports Bedrock Nova: audit provider message transform, add model detection (regex or catalog lookup), implement image move logic (tool-result -> user message), add unit tests (mock Bedrock 400 on tool-result image, verify transform moves image to user message), integration test with mock Bedrock endpoint. SKIP IF Alexi does not support Bedrock Nova yet.

- **Source**: https://github.com/Kilo-Org/kilocode/pull/14524 (Bedrock tool-result images), /home/runner/work/alexi/alexi/src/providers/transform.ts (provider message transform), /home/runner/work/alexi/alexi/src/providers/modelCatalog.ts (model catalog), /home/runner/work/alexi/alexi/src/providers/bedrock-model-id.ts (Bedrock model ID handling)

- **Category**: provider (Bedrock, message transform)

#### 4. Kilocode serve shutdown deadline SMALL ~2-3h (cli, server)

- **What**: Kilocode PR #14830 (merged 2026-10-09) bounds serve shutdown after signals. Commit title: "fix(cli): bound serve shutdown after signals". `kilo serve` installs SIGINT/SIGTERM handlers that call `server.close()` + `await killAllTracked()` (background processes). If a background process hangs (unresponsive MCP server, stuck shell), shutdown waits forever. Docker/systemd send SIGKILL after 10s, killing process tree ungracefully. Fix: wrap shutdown in `Promise.race` with 30s timeout, force `process.exit(0)` after timeout, log which processes timed out. Graceful shutdown completes in <1s for normal cases, 30s deadline catches hangs.

- **Why**: Alexi has `server` command (`src/cli/commands/server.ts`). Check if `server start` installs SIGINT/SIGTERM handlers (grep for `process.on('SIGINT')` in `server.ts`). Alexi program.ts (L49-53) installs one-shot shutdown (`killAllTracked()` + `shutdownTracing()`) but no deadline. Kilocode pattern: (1) wrap `server.close()` + `killAllTracked()` in `Promise.race([shutdown, timeout(30000)])`, (2) on timeout, log timed-out process IDs, call `process.exit(0)`, (3) normal shutdown path calls `process.exit(0)` after cleanup. Alexi equivalent: audit `src/cli/commands/server.ts` for SIGINT/SIGTERM handlers (if exists), wrap shutdown in `Promise.race` with 30s timeout (use `setTimeout` + `reject`), log timed-out processes before force exit, test with mock hanging background process (e.g. `sleep infinity` via background_process tool, send SIGINT, verify 30s deadline triggers force exit). SMALL ~2-3h: audit server shutdown handlers, add 30s deadline via Promise.race, log timeout, test with hanging process.

- **Source**: https://github.com/Kilo-Org/kilocode/pull/14830 (serve shutdown deadline), /home/runner/work/alexi/alexi/src/cli/commands/server.ts (server command), /home/runner/work/alexi/alexi/src/cli/program.ts L49-53 (one-shot shutdown, no deadline), /home/runner/work/alexi/alexi/src/tool/tools/background-process.ts (killAllTracked)

- **Category**: cli (server, shutdown)

- **Size**: SMALL ~2-3h (audit server SIGINT/SIGTERM handlers, wrap shutdown in Promise.race with 30s timeout, log timed-out processes, test with hanging background process)

#### 5. Cline agent_error hook dispatcher SMALL ~2-3h (hooks, dispatcher)

- **What**: Cline PR #14945 (merged 2026-10-09) accepts agent_error hook events in hook command. Commit title: "fix(cli): accept agent_error hook events in the hook command". `cline hook` command dispatches hook events to external handlers (command, http, script). Shared hook schema (`HookEvent` type) includes `agent_error` (emitted when agent run fails). Hook command dispatcher had no case for `agent_error`, so valid payloads fell through to default branch, command exited 1 without JSON response. Fix: add `case 'agent_error':` that returns `{}` like other agent events (`SessionStart`, `SessionEnd`, `Stop`). PR adds first unit tests for hook command (dispatcher coverage).

- **Why**: Alexi has hooks (`src/hooks/index.ts` 956 lines). Check `HookEvent` type definition (L24-32) includes `Error` event (not `agent_error`, naming may differ). Audit hook dispatcher in `src/hooks/index.ts` or `src/cli/commands/` (if hook command exists). Cline issue: dispatcher switch statement missing case for valid event type. Alexi equivalent: (1) audit `HookEvent` type for all declared events (`SessionStart`, `SessionEnd`, `PreToolUse`, `PostToolUse`, `PostToolUseFailure`, `PermissionRequest`, `Stop`, `Error` per L24-32), (2) audit hook dispatcher (likely `executeHook` function or CLI `hook` command handler), (3) verify dispatcher has case for EVERY event type, (4) add missing cases if any (return `{}` or appropriate response), (5) add unit tests (mock hook payload for each event type, verify dispatcher returns success). SMALL ~2-3h: audit HookEvent type, audit dispatcher switch/if-else, add missing cases if any, unit tests for each event type.

- **Source**: https://github.com/cline/cline/pull/14945 (agent_error hook dispatcher), /home/runner/work/alexi/alexi/src/hooks/index.ts L24-32 (HookEvent type: SessionStart, SessionEnd, PreToolUse, PostToolUse, PostToolUseFailure, PermissionRequest, Stop, Error), /home/runner/work/alexi/alexi/src/cli/commands/ (check for hook command)

- **Category**: tools (hooks, dispatcher coverage)

- **Size**: SMALL ~2-3h (audit HookEvent type for all events, audit dispatcher for missing cases, add missing cases if any, unit tests for each event type)

#### 6. Cline provider API key from environment SMALL ~2-3h (TUI, config)

- **What**: Cline PR #14926 (merged 2026-10-09) treats provider API key from environment as configured. Commit title: "fix(cli): treat a provider API key from the environment as configured". Cline TUI startup check calls `isProviderSettingsUsable` to verify provider is ready. Check rejected providers with API keys from environment (e.g. `OPENROUTER_API_KEY`) when key was not saved in config. User with `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` set could not start TUI without saving key to config. Fix: startup check now accepts environment keys for providers that declare exactly one environment variable (OpenRouter, Anthropic, OpenAI). Providers with multiple environment variables (Bedrock `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID` + `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`, Vertex `GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS`) unchanged. Nothing is persisted — environment key remains transient.

- **Why**: Alexi TUI in `src/cli/tui/` likely has startup check. Audit for provider config validation (grep for `isProviderSettingsUsable` or equivalent in TUI entry point). Cline issue: startup check required config file entry even when environment variable present. Alexi equivalent: (1) audit TUI startup check (`src/cli/tui/App.tsx` or `src/cli/interactive.ts`), (2) identify provider validation logic (check if API key required), (3) update validation to accept environment keys (check `process.env.OPENROUTER_API_KEY`, `process.env.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, etc. before rejecting provider), (4) limit to single-env-var providers (OpenRouter, Anthropic, OpenAI yes; Bedrock, Vertex no), (5) test TUI starts with `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` set but no config file entry. SMALL ~2-3h: audit TUI startup check, identify provider validation, add environment key check for single-env-var providers, test TUI starts with env key only.

- **Source**: https://github.com/cline/cline/pull/14926 (provider API key from environment), /home/runner/work/alexi/alexi/src/cli/tui/App.tsx (TUI entry), /home/runner/work/alexi/alexi/src/cli/interactive.ts (interactive REPL), /home/runner/work/alexi/alexi/src/providers/auth.ts (provider auth)

- **Category**: config (TUI, provider validation)

- **Size**: SMALL ~2-3h (audit TUI startup check for provider validation, add environment key check for single-env-var providers, test TUI starts with OPENROUTER_API_KEY only)

#### 9. Kilocode Windows drive-root startup REFERENCE-ONLY (vscode)

- **What**: Kilocode PR #14519 (merged 2026-10-09) starts backend in Windows drive-root workspaces. Commit title: "fix(vscode): start the backend in Windows drive-root workspaces". VSCode extension backend start failed when workspace was Windows drive root (e.g. `C:\`, `D:\`). Backend spawn used workspace path as cwd, Node.js spawn rejected drive root as cwd (must be `C:\` with trailing backslash, not `C:`). Fix: normalize drive root to `C:\` before spawn.

- **Why**: Alexi is CLI + TUI, no VSCode extension. Not applicable. REFERENCE-ONLY: if Alexi adds editor integrations (VSCode, JetBrains), remember to normalize Windows drive root before spawning child processes.
